title: Finish collaboration with evidence
subtitle: Move from AI says done to I know why I accept it.
concept: Review diffs, acceptance results and verification evidence before accepting, correcting or splitting the task further.
intuition: For a renovation handover, inspect the room rather than just reading the contractor's done message.
objectives: Read changed files and key diffs, explaining their relation to the goal.
After acceptance, leave a focused commit and handoff notes; otherwise return specific evidence.

body.title: Read diffs from the problem outward
body.text: Inspect file scope, then key changes. Title validation should include trimming, rejection and feedback, with matching tests. A new framework, broad renames or lockfile changes need a reason. Ask for concrete inputs through unfamiliar syntax, then try them yourself.

body.title: Do not adjust tests to suit incorrect code
body.text: If the limit remains 80, deleting the rejection test at 81 is not a fix. A confirmed new standard may change tests, but must preserve complete boundary coverage. Instead of still broken, provide input, actual and expected results, and reproduction steps.

body.title: Leave handoff records
body.text: Commit accepted changes with a clear purpose and record implementation, checks and gaps. Future sessions should read those records. Track accepted, awaiting checks and deferred separately. Read, tested and deployed are distinct states; one done label should not hide them.

formalDefinition.text: Review diffs, acceptance results and verification evidence before accepting, correcting or splitting the task further.
conditions: For small personal learning projects. In shared repositories, follow the team's conventions.
This method produces checkable evidence; it cannot guarantee arbitrary AI output is correct.

workflow: Read changed files and key diffs, explaining their relation to the goal.
Follow predefined acceptance cases and check real results and gaps.
After acceptance, leave a focused commit and handoff notes; otherwise return specific evidence.

workedExamples.title: Review a whitespace fix
workedExamples.problem: The change adds a large dependency. Is it reasonable?
steps: Check whether trim and existing validation suffice.
Ask for the dependency's necessity and maintenance cost.
Remove unrelated changes if unnecessary, then reverify.
workedExamples.answer: The current functions can implement this rule. Explain the dependency's specific purpose; if unnecessary, retain the existing dependency structure. Rerun existing tests and report results rather than deleting tests to reduce files.

workedExamples.title: A useful correction request
workedExamples.problem: Items disappear after refresh. How should you report it?
steps: Provide URL, console details and checked scope.
workedExamples.answer: At http://127.0.0.1:5180, adding Learn Git displays it, but refresh empties the list. It should persist. Inspect saving, loading and error handling; explain the cause and make a minimal fix without adding synchronization.

commonMistakes.claim: Accept every diff you do not understand.
commonMistakes.correction: Choose key behavior, ask for concrete-input explanation and verify it yourself.
Decide whether implementation violates requirements or requirements were deliberately changed; green alone is not the goal.

practice.problem: Twenty files changed for one color. What first?
practice.answer: Inspect files and diffs, explain unrelated changes and reduce to necessary style changes.
solution: Many files are not automatically wrong, but every change needs a reason.

practice.problem: How can the agent explain an unfamiliar condition?
practice.answer: Trace three spaces and an ordinary title through the branch, stating intermediate values and whether an item is created.
solution: Do not settle for abstract praise.

practice.problem: The limit is 80 but its test was deleted. Accept?
practice.answer: Not just because results are green. Restore boundary coverage and fix behavior, unless a confirmed new standard has complete replacement tests.
Whitespace rejection is fixed and committed. npm test passed and browser feedback was checked. Other browsers and concurrent tabs remain unverified.
solution: The next task can continue from it.

learningCheck.question: What supports accepting a change?
choices: Relevant diffs, acceptance results and actual tests
feedback: This evidence can be compared with the goal.
Line count has no direct relation to user outcomes.

interactiveVisual.prediction: If tests pass, must you still review diffs?

steps.question: A color change adds a data migration.
feedback: The link between data changes and styling is unclear.
Existing data may be changed unintentionally.

steps.question: Tests were deleted and results are green.
feedback: Green may reflect a lowered standard.

steps.question: You find a refresh failure. How next?
choices: Give reproduction, actual and expected results
feedback: No new diagnostic evidence is supplied.
The next change can target a concrete failure.

interactiveVisual.followUp: Fill a correction brief in the lab with evidence instead of still broken.

promptTemplate.goal: Diagnose and fix list loss after refresh within existing scope.
promptTemplate.context: At http://127.0.0.1:5180, adding Learn Git works, then refresh empties the list. Persistence is expected. I will attach the original error.
promptTemplate.scope: Inspect save/load and origin first. No site rewrite, new service or overwriting old data.
promptTemplate.acceptance: At the same URL, ordinary additions survive refresh; whitespace remains rejected; failed writes clearly say data was not saved.
promptTemplate.verification: Repeat reproduction, run rule tests and inspect related errors. State anything you cannot execute.
promptTemplate.delivery: Root cause and evidence, minimal fix, actual verification and remaining risks.
